data.headline: Thirty-year Treasury yield falls to 5.31% as its spread over the ten-year widens
data.summary: The thirty-year Treasury yield fell nine basis points from Thursday to Friday, while the ten-year yield fell twelve. The gap between them widened from 36 basis points on November 19 to 39 on November 20.

bull.text: The thirty-year benchmark declined from 5.40% to 5.31%. A decline in the yield on a long bond supports its price, all else equal.

bear.text: Asset managers reduced their net long in Treasury bond futures from 394,990 to 371,794 contracts in the week to November 17. This reduction preceded Friday’s move in yields.

watch.text: The ten-year yield ended Friday at 4.92%. If the ten- and thirty-year yields keep moving at different speeds, TLT’s longer maturities make the thirty-year reading particularly relevant.

limitations: Treasury par yields and weekly bond-futures positions cover different instruments and dates. Measuring TLT’s own return requires the ETF’s regular-session open and close and the applicable distribution history.
